speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you have been experiencing these nosebleeds and skin spots, and have you noticed any bleeding from your gums or in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the child experienced any recent infections, fevers, or fatigue, and have you noticed any swelling in his abdomen or enlarged lymph nodes? I also need to check if he has had any bone pain or if the bleeding is difficult to stop.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal platelet count and coagulation profile, I suspect a primary hemostasis defect like von Willebrand disease. Have you noticed if the bleeding worsens with minor trauma, and is there any family history of similar bleeding disorders?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical issues. Up-to-date on vaccinations. Social history: Attends preschool. Lives with parents and one older sibling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any personal or family history of easy bruising, heavy menstrual bleeding, or prolonged bleeding after dental work? I also need to know if the child has had any recent viral illnesses or if he is currently taking any medications, especially aspirin or NSAIDs.
